title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: creating Judas the reprobate is not creating him that he may be damned — as feeding a thief sentenced to die is not feeding him that he may die
latin: Deum recte dici agere propter intentum aliquem finem, cum rebus talem dat naturam ut sint propter talem finem: Deus autem creando Judam non dedit illi naturam ad damnationem ordinatam: Falso igitur statuitur creatio Judae reprobati habere hanc intentionem, ut medium sit quod ad damnationem provehatur. Aliud enim est creare hominem reprobatum et ob demerita sua damnandum, aliud creare ut damnetur; sicut aliud est alere, vestire, solari latronem damnandum, aliud haec facere ut damnetur.
pass_a: God is rightly said to act on account of some intended end, when he gives unto things such a nature that they are for such an end: But God in creating Judas did not give him a nature ordained unto damnation: Falsely therefore is it established that the creation of Judas the reprobate has this intention, that it be a medium which is advanced unto damnation. For it is one thing to create a man reprobate and to be damned on account of his demerits, another to create that he may be damned; as it is one thing to feed, clothe, comfort a thief to be damned, another to do these things that he may be damned.
pass_b: God is rightly said to act for some intended end when he gives things a nature ordered to that end. But in creating Judas God did not give him a nature ordained to damnation. So it is false to hold that the creation of Judas the reprobate has this intention — that it be a medium advanced toward damnation. It is one thing to create a man reprobate and to be damned for his demerits; another to create him that he may be damned — as it is one thing to feed, clothe, and comfort a thief sentenced to die, another to do those things that he may die.

lemmas.gloss: create reprobate ≠ create in order to damn
feeding condemned thief ≠ feeding so he may die

title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: God creates in time those not predestined to beatitude — creation's proper end is communication of good, not damnation as intended scope
latin: Creat ergo Deus in tempore, quos ab aeterno minime praedestinavit ad beatitudinem, quos praevidit sua culpa ad interitum ruituros voluntarium, quos decrevit permittere ut inciderent in hanc miseriam sempiternam: sed interim creatio hominum (quae ordine decernendi haec omnia praecessit) habuit proprium suum finem, Dei gloriam in diffusione ac communicatione boni, non damnationem eorundem, quae habenda est eventus consequens creationem reprobatorum, non scopus intentus a Deo creante.
pass_a: God therefore creates in time those whom from eternity he by no means predestined unto beatitude, whom he foresaw by their own fault about to rush unto voluntary destruction, whom he decreed to permit that they should fall into this everlasting misery: but meanwhile the creation of men (which in the order of decreeing preceded all these things) had its own proper end, the glory of God in the diffusion and communication of good, not their damnation, which is to be held an event following the creation of the reprobate, not a scope intended by God creating.
pass_b: So God creates in time those he from eternity did not predestine to beatitude — whom he foresaw would by their own fault rush to voluntary ruin, whom he decreed to permit to fall into this everlasting misery. Yet men's creation (which in the order of decreeing preceded all that) had its own proper end: God's glory in the diffusion and communication of good — not their damnation, which is to be held an event following the creation of the reprobate, not a scope intended by God as creator.

lemmas.gloss: damnation follows; not creating's intended aim

title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: Scripture sounding as if God created some unto contumely is to be read permissively — vessels of contumely by not adding special grace
latin: Denique, si quae loca Scripturae in hunc sensum sonare videantur, quasi Deus creasset aliquos in contumeliam et perditionem, sunt, meo quidem judicio, interpretanda permissive. Creat enim indies, quos secundum decretum non-electionis seu reprobationis permittit fieri vasa contumeliae, non apponendo illam specialem gratiam quae faceret eos vasa honoris.
pass_a: Finally, if any places of Scripture seem to sound unto this sense, as if God had created some unto contumely and perdition, they are, in my judgment at least, to be interpreted permissively. For he creates day by day those whom according to the decree of non-election or reprobation he permits to become vessels of contumely, by not applying that special grace which would make them vessels of honor.
pass_b: And last: wherever Scripture seems to speak as though God had fashioned some for disgrace and ruin, I judge those places to be taken permissively. Day by day he brings into being those whom, under the decree of non-election or of reprobation, he suffers to turn into vessels of contumely — withholding the special grace that would have made them vessels of honor.

lemmas.gloss: vessels of contumely by withholding special grace

title: Cap. IX Arg. 10: if election and reprobation hang on mere liberty of will, Gospel preaching to the reprobate becomes from God's precise intention a ministry of condemnation
latin: Si ponamus electionem et reprobationem ex mera libertate Divinae voluntatis pendentem, et non ex discriminatis actibus ipsorum electorum et reprobatorum (puta horum poenitentia, illorum impoenitentia, horum fide perseverante, illorum finali infidelitate): tum Evangelii praedicatio quoad reprobatos ex proxima et precisa Dei intentione erit ministerium condemnationis, et non proponetur ipsis ex prima Dei intentione ad salutem ipsorum operandam, sed ut medium exsequendo decreto reprobationis damnationi subordinatum. At hoc directe cum ministerio Evangelii pugnat, utpote quod ex prima Dei intentione est ministerium vitae.
pass_a: If we place election and reprobation as hanging from the mere liberty of the Divine will, and not from the discriminated acts of the elect and reprobate themselves (namely the penitence of these, the impenitence of those, the persevering faith of these, the final unbelief of those): then the preaching of the Gospel as to the reprobate from the nearest and precise intention of God will be a ministry of condemnation, and will not be proposed unto them from the first intention of God unto working their salvation, but as a medium in executing the decree of reprobation subordinated unto damnation. But this directly fights with the ministry of the Gospel, inasmuch as from the first intention of God it is a ministry of life.
pass_b: If we set election and reprobation as hanging on mere liberty of divine will — not on the differing acts of elect and reprobate themselves (these' penitence, those' impenitence; these' persevering faith, those' final unbelief) — then Gospel preaching toward the reprobate, from God's nearest precise intention, will be a ministry of condemnation, and will not be set before them from God's first intention to work their salvation, but as a medium subordinated to damnation in executing the reprobation decree. That fights the Gospel ministry head-on, since from God's first intention it is a ministry of life.

lemmas.gloss: adversaries: absolute reprobation makes Gospel condemnatory
Gospel by first intention is ministry of life

title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: Major's consequence invalid — not everything later done about the non-elect flows from absolute reprobation; Vasquez: some effects are of common providence
latin: Consequentiam Majoris invalidam esse respondemus; atque in hoc falli adversarios affirmamus, quod posito absolutae reprobationis decreto quasi consequens assumunt, ex hoc decreto manare quicquid postea circa hosce non-electos sive reprobatos peragitur. At e contra recte observavit Vasques, Nec in praedestinato nec in reprobato omnem effectum providentiae Dei esse praedestinationis aut reprobationis, sed aliquem esse effectum communis providentiae, In 1. quaest. 23. artic. 4. cap. 4. disp. 93.
pass_a: We answer that the consequence of the Major is invalid; and in this we affirm the adversaries are deceived, that the decree of absolute reprobation being posited they assume as a consequence that from this decree flows whatever afterward is done about these non-elect or reprobate. But on the contrary Vasquez rightly observed, That neither in the predestined nor in the reprobate is every effect of the providence of God an effect of predestination or of reprobation, but that some is an effect of common providence, In 1. quaest. 23. artic. 4. cap. 4. disp. 93.
pass_b: We answer that the Major's consequence is invalid. The adversaries err in this: having posited absolute reprobation, they take it as following that whatever is later done about these non-elect or reprobate flows from that decree. Vasquez rightly notes the contrary: neither in the predestined nor in the reprobate is every effect of God's providence an effect of predestination or reprobation — some is an effect of common providence (In 1 q.23 a.4 c.4 disp. 93).

lemmas.gloss: some providence effects are common, not reprobation

title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: God knows Gospel benefits will harm reprobates and decreed not to add softening grace — yet preaching is not from primary intention a medium of damnation
latin: Concedimus quidem, Deum scire Evangelii praedicationem, aliaque omnia sua beneficia hisce reprobatis fore noxia; concedimus insuper, nullius reprobati voluntatem tam feram tamque intratabilem esse, quin possit Deus illam ad fidem et poenitentiam (hoc est, ad obediendi effectum) emollire; concedimus denique, Deum decrevisse apud se hisce reprobatis non apponere illam gratiam specialem et efficacem, qua emollirentur: Sed hisce omnibus positis negamus, aut Evangelii praedicationem, aut illam parcitoris et communioris gratiae donationem ex primaria et proxima intentione damnandi proponi, aut tanquam media damnationi subordinata judicari oportere. Non enim debemus ex praevisione, aut permissione Dei, aut ex eventu subsequente inferre primariam Dei intentionem, et mediorum subordinationem ad talem eventum producendum spectasse.
pass_a: We grant indeed that God knows that the preaching of the Gospel, and all his other benefits, will be noxious unto these reprobate; we grant further that the will of no reprobate is so wild and so intractable that God cannot soften it unto faith and penitence (that is, unto the effect of obeying); we grant finally that God has decreed with himself not to apply unto these reprobate that special and efficacious grace by which they would be softened: But all these things being posited we deny that either the preaching of the Gospel, or that gift of a scantier and more common grace, is proposed from a primary and nearest intention of damning, or ought to be judged as media subordinated unto damnation. For we ought not from foresight, or permission of God, or from a following event to infer that the primary intention of God, and the subordination of media, looked unto producing such an event.
pass_b: We grant God knows Gospel preaching and his other benefits will be harmful to these reprobates. We grant further that no reprobate's will is so wild and intractable that God cannot soften it to faith and penitence — that is, to the effect of obeying. We grant finally that God has decreed with himself not to apply to these reprobates that special efficacious grace by which they would be softened. All that granted, we still deny that Gospel preaching, or that gift of scantier commoner grace, is proposed from a primary nearest intention of damning, or ought to be judged media subordinated to damnation. From foresight, or God's permission, or a following event, we may not infer that God's primary intention, and the subordination of media, aimed at producing that event.

lemmas.gloss: knows harm; withholds softening grace — still not intent to damn by preaching
